summary: Olivia Chow's Instagram record on housing centers on affordability, renter protection, and a public role for the City in building homes. Chow frames Toronto as facing a housing and homelessness crisis driven by surging rents, renovictions, and a decade of inaction, and supports having the City act as a public developer rather than relying on private developers alone. Specific commitments include 25,000 new rent-controlled homes over 8 years on city-owned land (the City Homes Plan), $100M/year to prevent renovictions, 1,000 new rent supplements with federal/provincial matching for 2,000 more, a Toronto Renters Action Committee, and support for community land trusts and culturally responsive housing. Earlier 2014 posts emphasize tenant rights, community housing, and opposing federal co-op funding cuts—positions consistent with the 2023 platform.

key_positions.stance: Supports building more affordable, rent-controlled housing in Toronto
Supports the City of Toronto acting as a public developer rather than relying on private developers alone
Supports stronger renter protections, including against renovictions, demovictions, and above-guideline rent increases
Supports community land trusts and community ownership models to keep homes affordable
Characterizes Toronto's housing situation as an affordability/homelessness crisis stemming from a decade of inaction
Supports culturally responsive and supportive housing, including for seniors and survivors of gender-based violence
Opposes federal cuts to co-op housing support

key_actions.action: Announced the City Homes Plan to build 25,000 rent-controlled homes over 8 years on city-owned land
Pledged $100M/year to prevent renovictions and secure affordable homes
Pledged to create 1,000 new municipal rent supplements and seek provincial/federal matching for 2,000 more
Pledged to establish a Toronto Renters Action Committee
Released a Secure Affordable Homes plan and a renters protection plan
Met with renters, seniors, community land trust members, and United Way partners to discuss housing
Announced an affordable housing plan during the 2014 mayoral campaign
